title: Advice to students: develop your own tone and style
summary: Simeon advises young players to find their own tone and style rather than copy others, noting New Orleans clarinetists each had a distinct style.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: What is their rhythm or their style?

Well I would advise all the students on any instrument, I mean, to try to develop their own style of playing and their own tone. It doesn't necessarily mean, I mean, to play jazz, that you have to copy another man's style, or copy his tone, probably played 40, 50 years ago. So try to develop your own tone and your own style of playing. All the clarinets in New Orleans had different styles. Johnny's style was different than Jimmy's. All of them, they had their own individual style. So I would advise all the youngsters coming up, try to develop their own style of playing and their own tone.
